about.toggle: About Digital Detox & Neurobiology of Focus
about.heading1: Neurobiology of Screen Time & Attention Fatigue
about.text1: Modern digital interfaces leverage variable reward loops, conditioning the brain to expect unpredictable stimulation. This constant micro-arousal overworks the prefrontal cortex and depletes directed attention capacity (Kaplan & Kaplan, Attention Restoration Theory). Stepping away from screens allows cognitive neural circuits to enter the Default Mode Network (DMN), facilitating creative consolidation and mental reset.
about.boundary: Mindful Wellbeing Boundary: This timer and breathing guide are designed for educational habits and productivity wellness. They are not a clinical intervention for compulsive technology addiction disorders.
about.dPillar1: Aligning focus intervals with natural 90-to-120 minute biological alertness cycles prevents chronic mental burnout.
about.dPillar2: Gazing at an object 20 feet away relieves ciliary muscle spasms and counters digital eye strain.
about.dPillar3: Deep paced diaphragmatic breathing shifts autonomic tone from sympathetic arousal to parasympathetic restoration.
about.dPillar4: Session logs, streaks, and timers exist solely on your local device with zero cloud tracking.
about.faq1Q: How does a digital detox break restore focus and dopamine balance?
about.faq1A: Frequent smartphone notifications trigger intermittent dopamine spikes that fatigue prefrontal executive control. Taking 5-to-30 minute screen-free breaks reduces mental clutter, lowers cortisol, and replenishes directed attention capacity.
about.faq2Q: What is the recommended screen break duration?
about.faq2A: Short 5-to-15 minute micro-breaks alleviate eye strain and refresh working memory. Longer 30-to-60 minute intervals align with biological ultradian cycles, providing deep restorative breaks that support sustainable focus and flow states.
about.faq3Q: Are my detox session times or records stored externally?
about.faq3A: Never. All timer countdowns, streaks, and session analytics are processed 100% locally within your device browser via localStorage. No personal logs or telemetry are transmitted to external servers.
